solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Sailor left with a legacy from sword fight?

parts.note: a wound from a duel leaves a scar behind, a lasting legacy

explanation.surface: A sailor comes away from a duel bearing a permanent mark.
explanation.walkthrough: A LASCAR is a sailor from India or Southeast Asia, a term from the days of British merchant shipping.
explanation.definitionFit: Lascar is a historical term for an East Indian seaman serving on European ships.

clue.text: Sin is risk when daughter is out of sight

indicators.note: the daughter letter disappears from view, so it is removed from the word for risk

parts.note: risk and danger are synonyms

explanation.surface: A moralist warns that sin becomes dangerous once a daughter slips from view.
explanation.definitionFit: Wrath is one of the seven deadly sins, so this fury counts as a sin.

clue.text: Part company with politician, one leading national organisation

indicators.note: one goes in front of the organisation, leading it in the order of letters

parts.note: MP, Member of Parliament, is the stock crossword politician
taken as written
NT is the National Trust, the British heritage charity

explanation.surface: A politician leaves a firm to become head of a national body.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Part company' looks like a phrase meaning separate, but 'Part' alone is the definition and 'company' starts the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A component is one piece or element of a larger whole, a part of it.

clue.text: It's rotten, what leading detective did

parts.note: someone leading a department ran it, so the leading done is RAN
CID, the Criminal Investigation Department, is the British police detective branch

explanation.surface: Something foul is linked to how the chief inspector behaved.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'what leading detective did' as what a person did in leading the detectives: RAN the CID.
explanation.definitionFit: Rancid describes fats or food gone off and smelling bad, that is spoiled.

clue.text: Corresponding from river location after work

indicators.note: the river and location pieces come after the work piece

parts.note: OP, short for opus, is a musical work
the Po is the great river of northern Italy
a site is a location

explanation.surface: Someone writes from a riverside spot once the job is done.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Corresponding' suggests writing letters, but it means matching across from something, as opposite sides do.
explanation.definitionFit: Opposite sides or numbers correspond to each other, facing as counterparts.

clue.text: Partially fruitless condition evident in old territory?

parts.note: being without one particular fruit is only partly fruitless, so free of oranges
a state is a condition

explanation.surface: Somewhere with a shortage of fruit turns out to be a former land.
explanation.walkthrough: The Orange Free State was a Boer republic in southern Africa, later a province of South Africa; the question mark flags the playful reading.
explanation.definitionFit: This nineteenth-century Boer republic no longer exists, so it is a former territory.

clue.text: Job with power to help, upfront expense having been met

parts.note: a post is a job or position
P is the abbreviation for power in physics
aid means help

explanation.surface: A position comes with influence to assist, and costs are covered in advance.
explanation.definitionFit: Postage paid in advance means the sending cost is already covered by the sender.

clue.text: Woman given conflicting directions for crossing America

indicators.note: the two compass points stand either side of America, as if spanning it

parts.note: S and N, south and north, are opposite compass points
USA is America

explanation.surface: A woman receives contradictory route advice for a trip across the States.
explanation.definitionFit: Susan is a common female first name, so it stands for a woman.

clue.text: Native unsettled by mean Brits

indicators.note: something unsettled is disturbed, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A local is disturbed by stingy British people.
explanation.definitionFit: A tribesman is a member of a tribe, a native of a particular people.

clue.text: Bigheads say nothing — aims can look dubious

parts.note: EG, for example, is what say means
O, the zero, is nothing

indicators.note: letters that look dubious are suspect and need rearranging

explanation.surface: Conceited people stay silent, as their goals appear questionable.
explanation.definitionFit: Bighead is slang for a conceited person, one obsessed with self-importance.

clue.text: Lose weight within judicious limits

indicators.note: the answer lies inside the run of letters of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A dieting tip: cut down on food, but sensibly.
explanation.definitionFit: To slim is to diet so as to shed body weight.

clue.text: Enduring children endlessly — that's the head man

indicators.note: the last letter of the word for children is cut off

parts.note: a brood is a family of young children
a king is the head man of a country

explanation.surface: A ruler puts up with his never-ending offspring.
explanation.walkthrough: BROOKING means tolerating, as in brooking no argument; 'Enduring' here is a verb form, not long-lasting.
explanation.definitionFit: To brook is to tolerate or put up with something, so brooking is enduring it.

clue.text: What is written is restricted

definitions.meaning: something written with a pen has been set down in ink
animals shut in a fold are confined, held in a pen

explanation.definitionFit: Penned means both written down with a pen and shut in an enclosure.

clue.text: River almost makes you sentimental

indicators.note: almost the whole word, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: the Tweed is a river on the border of England and Scotland

explanation.surface: A Scottish waterway nearly brings out your soppy side.
explanation.definitionFit: Twee is British for excessively quaint, sweet or sentimental.

clue.text: Like loaf of bread as starters, main course and pudding?

definitions.meaning: a brown loaf made from unrefined flour including the bran
all three courses together are an entire dinner

explanation.definitionFit: Wholemeal describes brown bread, and a complete dinner of all courses is a whole meal.

clue.text: Hoopla? A reasonable object of ridicule

definitions.meaning: a fairground game in which rings are thrown over prizes
someone legitimately open to attack or mockery

explanation.definitionFit: Fair game is an idiom for a legitimate target, and hoopla is a game at a funfair.

clue.text: Beautiful musical instrument somewhere in Wales

parts.note: glam, short for glamorous, means beautiful
the organ is a musical instrument

explanation.surface: A lovely instrument is played at a Welsh location.
explanation.definitionFit: Glamorgan is a historic county in south Wales, home to Cardiff.

clue.text: King maybe on horse, one turning up in woollen jacket

indicators.note: in a down clue the card piece sits on top of the rest

parts.note: a king is one example of a playing card

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means the letters are read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a nag is an old horse
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A monarch on horseback appears in a knitted top.
explanation.definitionFit: A cardigan is a knitted woollen garment that buttons down the front.

clue.text: Couple admitting love at sporting event

indicators.note: the word for couple lets the other letters inside

parts.note: a brace is a pair, a couple
love is zero in tennis, written as O
taken as written

explanation.surface: Two people let romance in at a sports occasion.
explanation.walkthrough: The Boat Race is the annual Oxford versus Cambridge rowing race on the Thames.
explanation.definitionFit: The annual university rowing contest on the Thames is a famous fixture in the sporting calendar.

clue.text: Spots knight lying in a church

indicators.note: the knight is lodged inside the church letters

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
N is the chess notation for knight

explanation.surface: A knight lies in state in a church.
explanation.definitionFit: Acne is a skin condition producing pimples, so it means spots.

clue.text: Solution offered by politicians we ridicule

indicators.note: the letters are supplied by the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Politicians propose a fix that we mock.
explanation.definitionFit: A solution to a problem or puzzle is its reply or result.

clue.text: Small creature given grub moaned

parts.note: a bee is a small creature
grub is slang for food, so given grub means fed

explanation.surface: A tiny insect received a larva to eat and complained.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grub' looks like an insect larva fed to the creature, but it is slang for food.
explanation.definitionFit: To beef is slang for complaining, so beefed means grumbled.

clue.text: Father chewing bird's bone

indicators.note: the father letters hold the bird in their mouth, around it

parts.note: Fr is the abbreviation for Father, a priest's title
the emu is a large flightless Australian bird

explanation.surface: Dad gnaws on a bird's bone.
explanation.definitionFit: The femur is the thigh bone, the longest bone in the body.

clue.text: Orchestra according to some sounding wrong, less authentic?

indicators.note: said aloud, at least in some accents, the words give the sound of the answer

parts.note: a sin is a wrong and phonier means less authentic

explanation.surface: An orchestra's playing is judged by some to be bad and fake.
explanation.walkthrough: SIN PHONIER sounds like SINFONIA only in non-rhotic accents that drop the final r, hence 'according to some'.
explanation.definitionFit: Sinfonia is used as the name of a small symphony orchestra.

clue.text: Princess given little house in mountainous part of America

parts.note: Princess Ida is the Gilbert and Sullivan operetta heroine
HO is a short form of house

explanation.surface: A princess gets a small home among the American mountains.
explanation.definitionFit: Idaho is a US state in the Rocky Mountains, a mountainous part of the country.

clue.text: Appear in bishop's office before Mass

indicators.note: the bishop's office piece comes ahead of the mass piece

parts.note: a bishop's see is his seat and jurisdiction
M is the symbol for mass

explanation.surface: Someone turns up at the bishop's office ahead of the church service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mass' looks like the church service but is M, the physics symbol for mass.
explanation.definitionFit: To seem is to appear or give an impression of being something.

clue.text: Person from Scotland or Wales aging terribly

indicators.note: terribly suggests something badly done, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone from Scotland or Wales is getting old badly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scotland or Wales' looks like a choice, but 'Wales' is anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A Glaswegian is a native of Glasgow, Scotland's largest city.

clue.text: Barrier around lake or foreign city

indicators.note: the barrier word goes around the other letters

parts.note: a fence is a barrier
taken as written

explanation.surface: A fence encircles a lake or some city abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: Florence is an Italian city, so foreign from a British setter's view.

clue.text: Managed amount of money said to be extortionate charge

indicators.note: said means the words are spoken out loud

parts.note: managed means ran, and an amount of money is a sum

explanation.surface: Someone who ran a sum of money calls it an outrageous fee.
explanation.definitionFit: A ransom is a sum demanded for releasing a captive, a payment extorted.
